Q: Python dictionary with threads A:

Python ensures multi-thread integrity of the data: that is, even if you never do any locks and attempt to do concurrent changes in the same subdictionaries, it won't crash the interpreter, nor will the dictionary itself become corrupted: you will always have the latest values that happened to be set, in any thread.

The runtime was built up on this premise per decades: it won't crash. Now that we have a "free threading" version of Python, without the GIL, which happens to actually allow more than one CPU core to run Python code in parallel, one of the "hard parts" was exactly to keep builtin data structures thread-safe.

That doesn't mean it will prevent data corruption due to two or more of your threads attempting changes in the dictionary expecting them to be "atomic". So, if more than one thread, for example, attempt to make changes to the same subdictionary there, you can have race conditions in your logic.

If your idea is that each subdictionary is handled by a single thread ("thread exclusive" as you put it), them, there is nothing to fear and noithing to change: the data structures will be fine.

But if you are passing the root dictionary around, and expecting the threads to create the subdictionaries, you have to take care so they don't try to add those under colliding keys - for that you could use a lock.

Q: Get value from dataframe transformation with regex A:

regex() gives array with all matching elements and you have to get first element from array.

You can use array_get(..., index) where index is a string:

use function Flow\ETL\DSL\{
    array_get,
}

// ...

    ->withEntry('id_detenteur', concat(

        array_get(ref('adresse_detenteur')->regex('/\d{5}/'), "0"),

        regex_replace("/ /", "", col('nom_prenom_detenteur'))
    ))

Output:

Generated ID: 70025VARENNELILA
Generated ID: 41600WOUTTERSMARINE
Generated ID: 41600WOUTTERSMATHILDE
Generated ID: DUCHENEJÉRÔME

Source code: Regex, ArrayGet

Q: Reproduce n-ary `vmap` from unary A:

Yes, vmap is able to map over a common dimension of multiple arguments. For example:

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

def f(x: jax.Array, y: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
  """Function with shape signature ([a],[b])->[c]"""
  assert x.ndim == y.ndim == 1
  return jax.numpy.concat([x, y])

n, a, b = 5, 3, 4

x = jnp.zeros((n, a))
y = jnp.zeros((n, b))

z = jax.vmap(f)(x, y)
assert z.shape == (n, a + b)

Q: Retrieve Billing Address from Stripe checkout session? A:

In 2020 when this question was asked, the accepted answer was the right way to extract the data. However, "...for sessions on or after March 30, 2022", the billing address can be found directly under customer_details.address as part of the Checkout Session object. Assuming you already have your checkout.session.completed event object...

const session = event.data.object
const billingDetails = session.customer_details

For reference, shipping details are found under session.collected_information.shipping_details, though the structure is slightly different.

Q: J1939 TP protocol A:

Yes, BAM (Broadcast Announce Message) is supported in J1939 Transport Protocol (J1939-21), but there are important constraints that explain why you're not seeing results with two nodes transmitting simultaneously.

BAM limitations with multiple nodes

BAM is a one-to-many broadcast transport protocol. The issue with your configuration is that BAM does not support concurrent transmissions of the same PGN from multiple source addresses on the same bus segment. When two nodes initiate BAM sessions simultaneously:

- Both send a TP.CM_BAM frame (PGN 60416) announcing the transfer

- The receiving nodes get confused about which data packets (TP.DT, PGN 60160) belong to which session

- J1939-21 does not define a mechanism to distinguish concurrent BAM sessions from different SAs for the same PGN

What J1939-21 actually supports

- One active BAM session per source address at a time

- Multiple concurrent BAM sessions from *different* source addresses are theoretically possible but rarely implemented correctly in stacks

- For peer-to-peer multi-packet transfers, use CMDT (Connection Mode Data Transfer) instead — it uses RTS/CTS handshaking and supports concurrent sessions properly

Recommended approach

If both ECUs need to transmit the same large PGN, stagger the transmissions or use different PGNs. In CANoe, check the J1939 Transport Protocol layer settings and verify each node's BAM timing: J1939-21 specifies a range of 50–200 ms between TP.DT frames, not a fixed value — the standard itself doesn't tightly define how that range should be applied, so different stacks pick different values within it (50 ms is the most common default). A mismatch between nodes within that allowed range can also produce symptoms like yours, so it's worth confirming what interval each node is actually using, not just whether it's compliant.

It's also worth checking the receiver-side T1 timeout (750 ms) — if concurrent BAM sessions are causing delays that push TP.DT spacing close to that limit, the receiver may be timing out and silently dropping the session, which would look like exactly the kind of intermittent failure you're describing.

The relevant document is SAE J1939-21 — Data Link Layer, section on Transport Protocol Functions.
